subject: physical-education
title: Reteach and varied practice: locomotor and non-locomotor sequencing under transfer
essentialQuestion: What can movement say that words cannot?
materials: Optional: two soft household objects may mark a path. Floor tape, cones, a track, and a gym are not required.
Use only soft, unbreakable household items that a trusted adult approves; imaginary equipment and paper planning are always valid substitutes.
movementCues: Begin in a ready position with a balanced base, soft knees, eyes up, and the travel path clear.
Move with quiet, controlled steps or wheel pushes and keep enough room to stop without crossing the boundary.
Change direction by slowing first, lowering the center of control, and pushing smoothly into the new path.
Finish under control inside the space; smooth starts, stops, and spacing matter more than speed.
Self-manage the task by rehearsing at low intensity, changing one variable at a time, and choosing control and repeatable technique over a maximal result.
ageAppropriateTechnique: Self-manage the task by rehearsing at low intensity, changing one variable at a time, and choosing control and repeatable technique over a maximal result.
spaceSetup: Clear a dry, non-slip area at least two arm-spans wide when available. Mark the boundary with visible household objects or imaginary lines, remove furniture, cords, pets, and breakables, and keep a stable chair or wall nearby if support helps. Low-space path: clear one arm-span while seated or standing and keep every movement in place.

optional: Optional: two soft household objects may mark a path. Floor tape, cones, a track, and a gym are not required.
householdSubstitutes: Use only soft, unbreakable household items that a trusted adult approves; imaginary equipment and paper planning are always valid substitutes.
equipmentRequirements.equalCreditNoEquipment: Equal-credit low-space option: travel in place or use seated arm patterns to show start, pathway change, controlled stop, and spacing decisions, then name the cue that kept the movement controlled. Full transfer credit requires a complete sequence plus evidence of recovering the count or phrase after an interruption. Performing, notating, storyboarding, or fully describing the sequence earns equal credit, and a safety pause or rest is responsible completion rather than failure.

safetyRules: Check the floor, ceiling, footwear or mobility supports, boundary, and any optional item before moving. Keep people, pets, furniture, cords, and breakables outside the boundary.
Use a self-selected easy-to-moderate challenge, breathe continuously, and choose control over speed, force, distance, or repetition.
Rest, reduce range or pace, use support, or choose the non-movement planning path at any time without losing credit.
Keep the pace below running indoors unless a trusted adult has approved a larger clear area. Use no jumping when the surface, ceiling, footwear, or balance support is uncertain.
stoppingRules: Stop immediately for pain, dizziness, unusual breathing difficulty, a head impact, or any movement that feels unsafe; tell a trusted adult.
Stop when a person, pet, object, or slippery surface enters the movement area. Reset the area before continuing.
After a head impact, injury, or symptoms that do not settle with rest, do not resume the activity until a trusted adult or qualified professional says it is safe.
accessibleAdaptation: Use the same cues while seated, supported by a stable chair or wall, using a mobility aid, working through a comfortable reduced range, or describing/gesturing the movement when movement is not appropriate. Work solo or with one trusted adult. The adapted path is assessed for the same control, decision, and explanation and earns equal credit. Full transfer credit requires a complete sequence plus evidence of recovering the count or phrase after an interruption. Performing, notating, storyboarding, or fully describing the sequence earns equal credit, and a safety pause or rest is responsible completion rather than failure.
lowSpaceNoEquipmentAlternative: Equal-credit low-space option: travel in place or use seated arm patterns to show start, pathway change, controlled stop, and spacing decisions, then name the cue that kept the movement controlled. Full transfer credit requires a complete sequence plus evidence of recovering the count or phrase after an interruption. Performing, notating, storyboarding, or fully describing the sequence earns equal credit, and a safety pause or rest is responsible completion rather than failure.
activitySteps: Setup: read the equipment, space, safety, stop, and transfer-evidence rules; clear the area and choose the standard or adapted path.
Prepare: begin with comfortable joint movements or a low-intensity rehearsal of the planned evidence while breathing normally.
Practice: apply the movement cues for locomotor and non-locomotor sequencing at a self-selected challenge, resting or reducing the range whenever control changes.

Apply: perform, simulate, diagram, gesture, or fully describe locomotor and non-locomotor sequencing under the authored transfer condition and preserve every required cue, decision, comparison, or revision. Full transfer credit requires a complete sequence plus evidence of recovering the count or phrase after an interruption. Performing, notating, storyboarding, or fully describing the sequence earns equal credit, and a safety pause or rest is responsible completion rather than failure.
Finish: transition to easy movement or rest, then name one safety check and one adjustment for next time. No score, measurement, photo, or recording is needed beyond the stated transfer evidence.
privacySafeScenario: Compose, refine, and perform a short original movement sequence for an audience of one trusted adult, or describe and notate it in full if the learner prefers not to perform.
studentTask: Learner works locomotor and non-locomotor sequencing through a complete sequence in which the learner safely pauses when needed and recovers a lost count or interrupted phrase without restarting the evidence from the beginning at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one. Full transfer credit requires a complete sequence plus evidence of recovering the count or phrase after an interruption. Performing, notating, storyboarding, or fully describing the sequence earns equal credit, and a safety pause or rest is responsible completion rather than failure.
knowledgeCheck: In one concise response, say which feature of locomotor and non-locomotor sequencing degraded first under the added demand, why, and what you would change before the next attempt.
completionCriteria: The learner clears or accurately describes the safe space and selects the standard, accessible, or no-equipment path for locomotor and non-locomotor sequencing.

The learner performs or fully models locomotor and non-locomotor sequencing under the authored transfer condition and supplies the stated cue, decision, comparison, or revision evidence. Full transfer credit requires a complete sequence plus evidence of recovering the count or phrase after an interruption. Performing, notating, storyboarding, or fully describing the sequence earns equal credit, and a safety pause or rest is responsible completion rather than failure.
The learner identifies the equipment choice (including none), one safety or stop rule, and one technique adjustment or next step.

A seated, supported, reduced-range, solo, low-space, no-equipment, simulated, diagrammed, or described version earns equal credit only when it preserves the same transfer evidence. Full transfer credit requires a complete sequence plus evidence of recovering the count or phrase after an interruption. Performing, notating, storyboarding, or fully describing the sequence earns equal credit, and a safety pause or rest is responsible completion rather than failure.
adaptationChoices: Use the same cues while seated, supported by a stable chair or wall, using a mobility aid, working through a comfortable reduced range, or describing/gesturing the movement when movement is not appropriate. Work solo or with one trusted adult. The adapted path is assessed for the same control, decision, and explanation and earns equal credit. Full transfer credit requires a complete sequence plus evidence of recovering the count or phrase after an interruption. Performing, notating, storyboarding, or fully describing the sequence earns equal credit, and a safety pause or rest is responsible completion rather than failure.
extensionChallenge: Design the next progression of locomotor and non-locomotor sequencing yourself, or coach the transfer condition to someone else so that they succeed with it — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
Sequences may be seated, small-range, hand-and-arm only, or built at any tempo. Notation, description, or storyboarding is an accepted alternative to performing.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice where locomotor and non-locomotor sequencing shows up outside the session under real conditions. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
This task never requires maximal effort, exercise as punishment, or movement through pain.
This task never requires gym access, specialized equipment, or a purchase; the no-equipment path earns equal credit.
